text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek started a two-day visit to Brussels on Monday where he is to meet his Belgian counterpart Jean-Luc Dehaene and general secretary of NATO Javier Solana.

- The Slovenian government, employers and unions on Monday started talks on a new social agreement to determine work benefits. The new agreement is expected to replace the current accord which will expire at the end of May.
- April pensions will remain unchanged for the third consecutive month, the Pension Fund said.
- Railway workers will go on strike for an hour on Tuesday morning, demanding higher salaries.

- The Ministry of Environment on Monday started procedures to remove about 15 tons of toxic waste from a cave near Podgrad, 100 kilometers west of Ljubljana, which could otherwise damage the water supply in the area.
- Slovenian basketball team Smelt Olimpija will start the Final Four EuroLeague tournament in Rome on Tuesday with a match against Greek Olympiakos.
- The Minister of Environment Pavel Gantar said the biggest ecological problems in Slovenia were securing water supplies, managing waste and reducing pollution in urban areas.
- Low temperatures last week, which fell to minus nine degrees Celsius, caused widespread damage to fruit trees in Slovenian coastal areas.
